nodes.summary: There is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ whose set of element orders equals that of the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.
nodes.title: Large alternating groups are recognizable by spectrum

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ with the same spectrum (set of element orders) as the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.107 on recognition of alternating groups by spectrum

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $G$ be a finite group whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$. Then every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.
nodes.title: Groups isospectral to an alternating group (Kourovka Problem 16.27)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every finite group $G$ whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$, every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.27 (statement)

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of the elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $m$ a natural number. A sequence $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ of subgroups of $G$ is a composition series of length $m$ if $s_0$ is the trivial subgroup, $s_m = G$, and for each $i < m$ the subgroup $s_i$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient $s_{i+1}/s_i$ is a simple group.
nodes.title: Finite composition series

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ be subgroups of $G$, and let $i < m$. The $i$-th factor of the chain is non-abelian if $s_i \cap s_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient group $s_{i+1}/(s_i \cap s_{i+1})$ is non-abelian, that is, it has elements $x, y$ with $xy \ne yx$. When $s_i \le s_{i+1}$, this quotient is $s_{i+1}/s_i$.
nodes.title: Non-abelian factor of a chain of subgroups

nodes.summary: Every group, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.80 positively (Mamontov and Jabara).
nodes.title: Groups with element orders $1$ to $7$ are isomorphic to $A_7$

nodes.summary: The proposition, asked by W. J. Shi, that every $OC_7$-group, that is, every group whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ (such a group is periodic), is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.80 ($OC_7$-groups)

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of natural numbers that are orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group
